market_view: South African shares slipped 0.4% on the week as a 2.2% Friday slide in gold and platinum miners, while the rand eased to R16.61/$ and the SA 10-year firmed to 8.73% on the medium-term budget, with the repo rate at 7.25% ahead of the 19 Nov MPC. In New York the S&P 500 fell 0.6% and the Nasdaq 2.0% on disappointing big-tech results, and the Fed held at 3.75-4.00% with two votes for a hike, keeping a December increase in play with September CPI at 3.7%. Gold fell 2.7% and platinum 7.6% while Brent stayed above $110 a barrel and iron ore held near $91/t, so investors should brace for higher-for-longer rates and favour cash-generative businesses with strong balance sheets over richly valued growth stocks.
